investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 6-node cluster reported only 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node could accept a new peer-pod VM at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never scheduled, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1883–1885) never reached the createAgent call, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) was fully violated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent workloads or leaked/zombie peer-pod VMs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests. Supported by all three sibling check messages reporting the same 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' condition (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If this pool was previously larger, a node label change, node removal, or taint addition could have shrunk available capacity without changing the VM resource limit itself.

Tertiary — peer-pod VM resource quota set too low for current load: the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource limit on the 2 eligible nodes may be configured at a value that is insufficient for the number of concurrent eval or production agent pods being scheduled.

Lower confidence — leaked or non-terminated peer-pod VMs holding resource slots: if prior eval runs or user sessions did not cleanly release kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (e.g., due to cleanup failures in withCleanup at run-status-probes.mjs line 1883), slots may be held by idle or orphaned pods.

Because the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) before it can poll state, the upstream pod scheduling failure prevented any agent from being created, which in turn caused the remote-agent-state check to produce zero evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing) and fail its expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 nodes that carry that resource. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. With no schedulable node available and no preemption victims eligible, every new remote-agent pod is stuck in Unschedulable state. The eval runner cannot advance past the createAgent step, so no evidence is collected and all three remote-agents checks fail. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 6-node cluster reported only 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never reached a running state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no node could accept a new peer-pod VM at the time of the eval run. Because the pod never scheduled, the runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1883–1885) never reached the createAgent call, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) remained absent and the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 254–259) was fully violated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-19 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the 6-node cluster had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which were already at capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any runtime evidence, leaving all 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) empty and the expected-output contract entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm (production-api environment) exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. At the time of the eval run, 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new remote-agent pod: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm", and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on both eligible nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for ~145 seconds before the eval timed out, producing no evidence and triggering the contract-gap failure. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods at the time of the eval run.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes in the 6-node cluster satisfy, making the effective schedulable pool very small and easily saturated.

TERTIARY — cluster under-provisioning: the 6-node cluster may have too few kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes to absorb concurrent eval probe traffic plus any live workload, causing transient but recurring scheduling failures.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — a recent change to eval runner scheduling or pod spec (not evidenced by any suspect change in sourceDiscovery.suspectChanges, which is empty) could have altered resource requests or affinity rules, but no such change is present in the supplied evidence.
